newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks take surprise dive eyeing Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks take surprise dive eyeing Wall St.

text.p: MADRID, July 18 (Reuter) 1515 GMT - Madrid stocks fell sharply on Friday, tracking a dive on Wall Street amid a futures expiry and taking the market by surprise, dealers said.
However the indices closed off lows, which neared four percent at one point, and concerns were not about medium term upside potential but rather volatility during the summer.
* General index down 15.03 points, 2.43 percent, to 603.29
* Ibex seen trading between 6,700 and 7,200 for rest of summer, with erratic movements expected
* Buyers seen coming back in clearly at these levels
The effect of increased volatility amid the futures expiry, along with news that key international brokerages were downgrading their weighting in Spain pressured the market lower.
But dealers agreed prospects further out remained rosy.
"We could still see further correction later in the summer, but it won't fall further than this. Medium term the prospects are good and fund managers have to buy," said a Banesto trader.
He added that part of the reason for today's fall was that investors are selling off before the key holiday period, locking in profits so far. But the market should not be unduly nervous.

"I think today's fall hurts because it's so long since we've had one. The problem for the moment is volatility. But there were buyers coming in at the end of the session. My reaction is pretty cold," he added.
Santander was one of this week's biggest losers, hit by downgrades from brokers after a strong run this year, dealers said. Shares came off lows however to end down 70 pesetas at 4,450.
BBV shed 350 pesetas to 12,810, also retracing part of a strong climb. Both banks are due to announce first half results before the end of July.
